description_en: Aśikharatemple on top of a fountain from circa 14th-15th century.The monument is situated in the locality of Guṭhīchaur, on the lower part of a hill and a hundred meters north of a rivulet flowing eastward.Theśikharatemple is oriented to the south-west. It has a square plan. The stone door frame is missing. The pediment has low-relief carvings of a circular spiral and a star-shaped motif. Likewise, the central vertical projections on the east facade has carvings of floral motifs. Thesanctumis empty. The usual pinnacle composed of two stoneāmalakasis missing.In front of theśikhara, to the south-west, is a fountain with a stone facing. The facing is carved with various mouldings,āmalakafriezes and seated couples (donors or deities).  Water comes out through two uncarved spouts. It is farmed on each side by platforms that have since been partly covered by earth. Only the platforms facings perpendicular to the the fountain's main facing are visible. Earth has been moved around the original basin to create a larger, half-buried one. Large stone beams that are probably ancient have been placed on the edges of the bassin.Dilli Raj Sharma has suggested that the purpose of a similar fountain in Dailekh was to provide fresh water for the worship of the temple's deity (Sharma 2012: p. 120).The association of aśikharatemple with a fountain is locally known as mugrāhā ordevaldhara. This type of construction was probably introduced from Uttarakhand (Chanchani 2019, 19). In west Nepal this type of plan is mainly met in the Jumla district and it has one occurence in the Dailekh and Mugu districts (Andolfatto 2019, 79-93). The geographic repartition may indicate a regional preference that could politicaly correspond to the Kalyāla dynasty of Jumla. This would date the site from c. 14th-15th century.
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)
